newsitem.title: GERMANY: Two in running to become German telecoms regulator.
newsitem.headline: Two in running to become German telecoms regulator.

text.p: A political advisory panel failed on Monday to recommend a single candidate to head Germany's planned post and telecommunications regulator, leaving two candidates still challenging for the post.
The 32-member regulatory council was split, with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) favouring former Alcatel SEL chairman Peter Landsberg, officials said.
Meanwhile, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) backed the candidacy of Dieter Scheurle, a top official in the Posts Ministry.
The Kohl government has the final say on who will take over the posts and telecoms regulatory body, which will start working when the Posts Ministry is dissolved at the end of 1997.

Germany, which last year privatised a quarter of Deutsche Telekom AG, is due to open its telecoms market to full competition next year. It also wants to sell off Postbank AG, which has been split off from the general postal service.
